School

Rationalism quotes

Rationalism holds that reason plays a primary role in knowledge—often defending a priori insight against pure empiricism.

36 passages · 7 voices in this archive selection

Overview

Early modern rationalists such as Descartes, Spinoza, and Leibniz built metaphysical systems from clear and distinct ideas or necessary truths. The label is comparative: few thinkers deny experience entirely, but they deny that all knowledge reduces to sensory impressions.

Historical notes

Seventeenth-century continental rationalism responds to skepticism and scientific change; later Idealism and analytic a priori debates continue related arguments.

Core ideas

  • Some truths are knowable by reason independent of particular sensory episodes.
  • Mathematics and logic model secure knowledge.
  • Metaphysics can be systematic and demonstrative.
  • Clear and distinct ideas (or sufficient reason) guide inquiry.

Thinkers in this archive

René Descartes , Baruch Spinoza , Karl Popper , Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz , Maimonides , Saadia Gaon , Judah Halevi

FAQ

What is rationalism in philosophy?

It is the view that reason is a primary source of knowledge, often including a priori truths.

Who are famous rationalists?

Descartes, Spinoza, and Leibniz are the classic early modern trio.
